about: Part of the reference catalogue: designed experiments from the book Process Improvement using Data, for testing that software
reproduces them. source: the citation, with the version and commit read. experiments: each worked example,
exercise and case study with its data (factors, responses, runs exactly as printed, in the printed order; or
data_source when the book's own code makes the runs) and expected: every number the book prints for it, as
printed text, with what it is, where it is printed (file, line, a quotation) and check: how to recompute it
(kind, term, model in the library's formula notation, runs, the 1-based positions used when not all), or
manual, the reason it is not recomputed, or disagreement, why a printed number does not reproduce. designs:
designs without responses, with the properties the book states. other: numbers the book prints that belong
to no one experiment. not_captured: what the readers left out, and why. Read with
process_improve.experiments.reference_catalogue; reproduce_reference_catalogue() recomputes every number that has a check.

'Position within case' is the column position in the printed table; it is not a run order. The book says the runs were taken from the larger data set (20 and 23 values). Case is the factor: A (low) is coded -1 and B (high) +1, so the effect of Case is ybar_B - ybar_A. Checked against the RST table (lines 188-192) and the arrays in the code (lines 210-211).

data_source.notes: The printed values are the first 8 values of TK104 and the first 9 of TK107 from this data set (the URL is printed in the R block at line 161, not in this subsection).

experiments.notes: The code-echo at line 223 comes from print(len(differences), f"{observed:.1f}", exceed, f"{1 - exceed / len(differences):.1%}"). 'exceed' counts splits with d > observed (strict); 79.6% is 1 - exceed/len. The 79.4% at line 200 is described as 'the probability of obtaining that value' using the t-distribution with 15 degrees of freedom; it reads as the cumulative probability P(t <= 0.8435), the counterpart of the 79.6% from the permutation count, not a two-sided p-value. The number 24,310 is also repeated in prose at lines 196, 198, 202 and 250. The histogram (with the scaled t-density and a vertical line at the observed difference) is shown only as a figure; the code builds it with 50 equal-width bins. The timing statements (lines 202, 254) are machine-dependent. Not in web/book-examples.json. The pooled-variance z of line 200 is the t-value of Case in the one-factor least-squares model fitted to the 17 runs (the equivalence the book shows in 'Using linear least squares models'): both are 0.8435 with 15 degrees of freedom, and twice the coefficient is ybar_B - ybar_A = 63.21. Checked while cataloguing by running the book's enumeration: 24,310 splits, 4956 above the observed difference, 79.6%; C(43, 20) is 960,566,918,220.

design.details: One factor at a time (COST / OFAT). Base point 346 K, 1.5 g/L. Temperature runs first (354 K, then 338 K, 330 K, 322 K); then substrate concentration at the best temperature, 330 K (1.75, 1.25, 1.0, 0.75 g/L). Budget of eight experimental runs, plus the base operating point. Four other variables (dissolved oxygen level, agitation rate, reaction duration, substrate type) are not changed.

S during the temperature runs is not restated in the text; 1.5 g/L is the base value held while only temperature changes. Yields are given only as phrases; the numeric yield of each run appears only in the figure image (COST-contours.png). The 'around 67%' is attached to run 3 because the text says the best temperature (330 K, run 3) boosted yield from 63% to around 67%; 69.7% is the yield at the final operating point 330 K, 0.75 g/L. Effects are per +16 K and per 0.5 g/L (low to high); the coefficients are half of them (-10 -> -5, -6 -> -3), which line 98 says explicitly ('They are the same, as long as we are careful to interpret them as the change over half the range'). Checks: a conditional effect (one factor at one level of the other) is the effect in the one-factor model on the two runs the book differences; average effects, coefficients and the baseline prediction use the book's model y = b0 + bT xT + bS xS + bTS xT xS (T*S). Cube plot, interaction plot and surface plot are images only.

Settings are in actual units (coded = false): the book's model matrix at lines 108-115 codes chemical P as -1 and Q as +1 (the factor's low and high), T 72 -> -1 and 100 -> +1, S 200 -> -1 and 400 -> +1. design.details: generate_omars(factors, n_runs=27, model='full_second_order', random_state=42): thirteen half-rows, their thirteen mirror images and one centre run (model_rank 15, expected_error_df 12). Run in two blocks (parallel runs) with each mirror pair kept in one block; the split of the thirteen pairs into seven and six chosen over all 1716 splits to minimise the largest |r| between the block indicator and the second-order columns. Three centre runs added (one to parallel run 1, two to parallel run 2) for thirty batches, 16 and 14 per parallel run, two centre runs per parallel run placed about a third and two thirds of the way through its run order; run order otherwise random (numpy default_rng(7)). Centre runs are runs 6, 12, 22 and 26.

data_source.notes: No data file: the responses are simulated by process_improve.simulation (BioreactorSimulator, BioreactorConfig) in the code blocks at lines 74-114, 224-246 and 272-283. within_batch_scale=0.7 x default; growth temperature 36.8 degC, 1.5-day ramp; batch seeds from np.random.default_rng(2026).integers(1 << 30, size=30); the second parallel run uses feed_substrate = 0.88 x default (12% less substrate, a new feed-medium lot). The 30-run plan and its titers are not printed; only the four centre runs' titers are (lines 287-292).

experiments.notes: All responses come from the package's simulator, so every printed number depends on the process_improve version (simulator kinetics, generate_omars). Text-block outputs (lines 285-292) are recorded as code-echo. The campaign table (lines 702-762) has no code in the RST (figure script doe/omars-worked-study-tradeoff.py only). Rounding stated or visible: centre-point p 0.1226 printed as 0.12 in prose (line 342); lack-of-fit p 0.07240 as 0.0724 (line 631); true optimum shift day 2.624 as 2.62 (lines 557, 613); 30.22 degC as 'near 30.2 °C' (line 614). The prose at lines 375-376 gives fifteen error df for the full model at thirty runs; the block shift was estimated from the same data before log_titer_adj was formed, and that degree of freedom is not deducted. The theory table header at line 850 refers to 'The property, from 5.16' (a section number). The 21- and 31-run designs in the variance-factor block (lines 783-791) use the study's factors with random_state=42; the 27-run value is the study design (without the three added centre runs). Line 139-140 says Quad 'from 10 runs' while the column figure alt text lists 'Quad from 11 to 19' (the figure shows odd run counts only).

design.details: Definitive screening design with fake factors: generate_design(factors, 'dsd', budget=17, random_state=1). Built from a conference matrix of order 8 (foldover/mirror image plus a centre run); the two columns not assigned to a factor are fake factors, giving 2 error df. Run in the laboratory reactor, where the heat limit does not apply. Analysed with analyze_omars(screen.design[names], y, quadratic_heredity='strong', interaction_heredity='strong') for each response.

data_source.notes: No data file: the design is generated in code (generate_design, random_state=1) and the responses are simulated by run_reactor(screen.design_actual) (line 176). The responses are simulated, not measured. Simulator (code block lines 89-142): true models in coded units (-1 low, +1 high) use only T, t and C: yield = 70 + 6 T + 4 t + 5 C + 2.5 T:C - 3 T^2 - 2 t^2 - 1.5 C^2; impurity = 1.6 + 0.2 T + 0.5 t + 0.1 C + 0.3 t^2 (as the dict TRUE_MODELS, line 115-119). Noise SD 0.5 on yield and 0.05 on impurity, in percentage points (NOISE_SD, line 120; also prose lines 80-81). Noise comes from rng = np.random.default_rng(2026) (line 137); run_reactor draws rng.normal(0, sd, n) for yield then impurity on every call, so the printed values depend on the call order: screen (17 runs), then stage 2 (16 runs), then the 3 confirmation runs. P, S and R appear in neither true model (line 79-80, 114).

experiments.notes: The run settings and the simulated observations are not printed; only the analysis results are echoed. Factor ranges come from the un-captioned list-table at lines 30-54 (table header 'Factor, Low, High'); R has no units. p-values are printed with f"{value:.2g}" (2 significant figures), so e.g. S '0.9' for yield is rounded. Selected terms are listed as active_main_effects + active_quadratics + active_interactions. The heat limit (0.04 T + C <= 9.5) does not apply to this laboratory stage; the 3 screening runs beyond it are noted as acceptable (line 225-226). The 'conference matrix of order 8' and '2 fake factors' appear in both prose (lines 151-152, 154) and code echo (line 161).

data_source.notes: No data file: the design is generated in code and the responses are simulated by run_reactor(stage2.design_actual) (line 344); confirmation runs by run_reactor on 3 copies of the optimum (line 445). The responses are simulated, not measured. Simulator (code block lines 89-142): true models in coded units (-1 low, +1 high) use only T, t and C: yield = 70 + 6 T + 4 t + 5 C + 2.5 T:C - 3 T^2 - 2 t^2 - 1.5 C^2; impurity = 1.6 + 0.2 T + 0.5 t + 0.1 C + 0.3 t^2 (as the dict TRUE_MODELS, line 115-119). Noise SD 0.5 on yield and 0.05 on impurity, in percentage points (NOISE_SD, line 120; also prose lines 80-81). Noise comes from rng = np.random.default_rng(2026) (line 137); run_reactor draws rng.normal(0, sd, n) for yield then impurity on every call, so the printed values depend on the call order: screen (17 runs), then stage 2 (16 runs), then the 3 confirmation runs. P, S and R appear in neither true model (line 79-80, 114).

experiments.notes: Runs, observations and fitted coefficients are not printed; only the echoed summaries are. Fits use coded T, t, C (stage2.design) with analyze_experiment(model='quadratic'). Desirability goals (lines 362-363, 370-373): yield maximize low 70 high 80; impurity minimize low 1.6 high 2.0; overall desirability is the geometric mean; the optimiser is confined to DesignRegion.from_dict(stage2.metadata['region']). Printed formats: residual SD .3f; optimum T .1f, t .1f, C .2f, heat .2f; predicted yield .2f, impurity .3f, desirability .3f; confirmation observations and interval limits .2f; ratio .1%. Simulation as written: time_points = np.arange(10); noise_sd = 0.03; ref = 1.0 - np.exp(-time_points / 2.0); ref = ref / ref.max(); tail = np.clip((time_points - 4) / 5.0, 0, None); tail = tail / tail.max(); truth = {compound: (drift, s_co, s_ph, s_tp)} = A (0.00, -0.05, -0.06, +0.02), B (0.05, -0.08, -0.10, +0.03), C (0.20, -0.20, -0.28, +0.12), D (0.30, -0.25, -0.30, +0.14), E (0.35, -0.10, -0.08, +0.05), F (-0.10, -0.15, -0.22, -0.10); rng = np.random.default_rng(20260710); amp = max(1.0 + 0.35 * concentration + s_co * co_solvent + s_ph * pH + s_tp * temperature, 0.05) on the CODED factor values; curve = amp * np.clip(ref + drift * tail, 0, None) + rng.normal(0, noise_sd, 10). peak = curves.max(axis=1) (line 528).

experiments.notes: Single simulated case study; every analysis uses the same 60 runs. Models, in order: (1) design scoring of the quadratic model (I-optimal 60 recorded here; I-optimal 48 and D-optimal 60/48 are design_only entries); (2) PLS main-effects model with reference coding (A dropped), 5 components; (3) ANOVA/OLS on the peak with sum coding C(compound, Sum) (F is the omitted level because levels are A..F); (4) PLS(3) on the peak vs OLS coefficients; (5) PLS interaction model on the full curve (5 and 3 components, LOO Q2); (6) T2/SPE diagnostics; (7) the same model under four codings; (8) score-match inversion, curve-match inversion, ground-truth check, constrained inversion. The coefficient table (lines 613-689) uses short term labels (cmpE, cmpA:pH, ...) for patsy columns like 'C(compound, Sum)[S.E]' and 'C(compound, Sum)[S.A]:pH'; under sum coding with levels A..F, F is the omitted level so A..E have their own contrasts; 14 middle terms are omitted from the table. process_improve's spe_ reports the SQUARE ROOT of SPE (lines 971-973), so the SPE values and the 6.6 limit are off-plane distances in scaled model-matrix units. Rounding: the ANOVA p-values are printed with format '.0e', F with '.0f'; R2 values to two decimals. Possible inconsistencies: (a) table row D (line 1349) gives concentration 3.8 umol/L while the echoed coded value is -0.38 (line 1290); whether this rounds to 3.8 or 3.9 depends on the unrounded coded value, so it may be fine. (b) Prose at lines 1377-1378 says the coding-invariant curve match 'closes most of that gap' between the score-match validated RMSE and the best match; for E the curve-match ground-truth RMSE (0.105, line 1719) is higher than the score-match validated RMSE (0.099, line 1361), while for B, C, D, F it is lower. (c) Echo at line 1015 prints the largest T2 as '22.0' while prose says '22'. (d) The 'Validated RMSE' column of the table at lines 1302-1368 and the 'Best match/Best emulation RMSE' values (tables at 1302 and 1727) are not printed by any code block: no block runs true_curve on compensate() output, and best_emulation() (line 1787) is only plotted, not scored. The reachable-set statements per coding (line 1417) come from figure colour-coding-inversion.png; no code block on the page computes the treatment/cell-means score-match inversions.
